*On the 3470 cycle of Chatay of the third age,  during the 45215 cycle (June  970) the false god Chôtuña of Mochykas was broken down, Guacrí(Càur) men captured the snake idol and after a short revolt, the small statue had it scales removed and the metal was melted and made into part of the sapa's crown.*
Fragment Guacrí Càur chronic.

[Spoiler=Cordone RP

The Plight of an Empire]

[b]Dareli[/b] 

There was Hardly a Sun by the time I rose out of bed, the sky remained mostly darkened, with the exception of twilight in the east. The Electrical lamps in my room were always on, although hardly bright enough to keep me out of sleep. I always had to wake up early,  the Empire required tending every day, even at such an hour it was necessary. 

Welar had never seen such troubling times before. The Empire remained stable, but it grew weaker every day in face of potential adversaries. Inostrancevia had the honor, the rare, and noble, honor, of never being colonized by a foreign power in its history. It had rather been isolated both by its extreme circumstances and its own leaders, leaving the nation who persisted in the Chaotic lands of the Far Northwest of Shamat to fend for itself. This isolation had brought about relative peace, but also issue. No one dared steered toward Inostrancevia thanks to some slightly exaggerated claims by fishermen who said that beasts hardly capable of putting down a small fishing boat could take down entire fleets. Of course, terrible beasts did persist in the waters off the coast, but infact they had been hunted extensively and were no longer a serious danger to anything but the smallest fishing boats.

Either way, his dynasty had ruled over Inostrancevia for generations, lasting since the mid 1500s, and had culminated with him, Welar Malakai. Inostrancevia was stable, but the rumors were speaking of increasing unrest beyond their borders, and while Inostrancevia wasnt too far behind technologically it lacked the resources to maintain a large and effective military.

Welar knew something had to change, the Empire had to open up.



Johann was kept up by his studies all night, he couldnt afford to fall asleep, heavy as his eyes were. His parents were absolute in their orders that he was to complete his studies as soon as possible, and in fairness they were probably right. They wanted him, his brothers and sister on the Council of Inostrancev as soon as possible. In order to do that, he needed to ace an exam. As a noble, he was entitled and guaranteed such a position with simply a test, although technically anyone could join the council they would need to spend years going through tests, training and conditioning to do so, and that costs money, which left out most of the population.

Even so, the Council was prestigious. It was basically second only to the grand emperor himself, and would discuss and decide numerous rules in the country.  The issue is however, that he personally only half-heartedly wanted to be on it. Most of the reason he wanted to was to please his parents, since they were the nobles of the upper peninsula after all, and the job was to make sure as much of the council as possible was filled by them.

But what he wanted in life was different. All he wanted to be was free, to be with his mount, to travel, to simply not be bound by borders that encompassed his world whole. Unfortunately, he had the displeasure of knowing that life was not that simple, and even for a noble like him there were limitations. Emperor Welar controlled all, even him, even his family, and the country was his servant.

But for now day had dawned, and he could call it in for his studies, because now he had to get to the grand training campus. He got out of his old wooden chair, hearing quite the scene downstairs, he guessed it was his brother Jamestz, who was always up early bragging about being first, and Sito, who claimed he would outpace him. He and his sister Janaciq were more reserved, Sito and Jamestz both had dragons, and could easily outpace him and his sister. His mount couldnt fly, and she drove a car.

So as he walked down the stairs he saw the door wide open, of course his brothers forgot to close the palace doors. He made sure to close them behind him and as he walked out he could see his brothers on their mounts, flying and fading into the distance as they raced to get to the campus. He sighed, walking to the stables so he could also get there.

Hey boy. He said to his mount as he opened the stable, The Dinosaur perked up, its feathery coat ruffling. He scratched his chin as he got onto the saddle.

Another day. He said as they set off to deal with the hell that was his brothers.

[quote=norrhollow;58814528]Three figures would be easily singled out from among the SummitONE operatives boarding the jeeps, all wearing what seemed to be lanyards indicating some degree of seniority within SummitONE's corporate hierarchy. All others were evidently military contractors, having been assigned to Sal-Baliz either as escorts or as part of their first envisioned contract with the Balizians.

Upon reaching Tazir Al Shinwar, the three figures would each carefully step out of the jeep, wordlessly nodding to each other as they allow the escorts to guide them further in.

"Well, about as fancy an introduction as you can get, honestly." The first of the three figures would take off his helmet and face coverings, revealing his long, brown hair and trademark blue eyes typical of the Norrhollower people. Reaching into his body armor, the man took out a pair of glasses, which he would put on to get a better look at the supreme leader. 

"Good day to you, Mr. Madhir." The man reached out his hand for a shake, grinning widely from ear to ear. "I'm Xavier Almstedt, President of the Almstedt Corporation and SummitONE Solutions. I'm delighted to be here today in front of your... amenable countrymen..."[/quote]

The supreme leader shook his hand and said Im glad you were able to make it, if you follow me I will take you to our current training facility. Madhir lead them into the compound and down a set of tight staircases. When they reached the bottom, they were presented with a large room. At the back of the room, targets with hundreds of bullet holes in them were set up. At the side was a rack of AK-47s. To the side was a bench, where three Sal-Baliz were sat eating.

[quote=sal-baliz;58819127]The supreme leader shook his hand and said Im glad you were able to make it, if you follow me I will take you to our current training facility. Madhir lead them into the compound and down a set of tight staircases. When they reached the bottom, they were presented with a large room. At the back of the room, targets with hundreds of bullet holes in them were set up. At the side was a rack of AK-47s. To the side was a bench, where three Sal-Baliz were sat eating.[/quote]
"About modest, all things considered." Almstedt coolly lamented. "Though not bad, I'm guessing it wasn't easy setting up shop in a place with uh... nasty acoustics..."

Almstedt looked at the walls of the training facility, then to the rack of revolutionary instruments, taking it all in. Though, as SummitONE's CEO, Almstedt's role was on the corporate side of things, not field work. For this, Almstedt turned to the two figures behind him, who had been quietly staring all around the place, seemingly in search of something.

"You two." Almstedt began. "Any grand opinions of our colleagues' faculties?"

The two SummitONE contractors looked at each other silently. Then, seemingly unprompted, one of them would take off their head coverings at last. Beneath the coverings was a young man, High Albic, likely in his later 20s or mid 30s, though with eyes that seemed over a decade older, and with silvering hair to match. Judging by his much heavier gear, he had to be a weapons specialist of sorts.

The contractor did not speak for a few seconds, instead taking a moment to breath in the stuffy air of the training grounds.

"Good day, Mr. Madhir. My name is Ulf Mayne, Commanding Officer and Regional Operations Manager of SummitONE Solutions Shamat and Team Leader for this operation" The man's voice was calm and monotonous, like a featureless and stony plain. "If I might give a comment... SummitONE Solutions has a large training facility in Stormhaven, which could be used as a template to renovate your current facilities. Notably, I'm seeing here a lack of hearing protection for your men, which would likely have some effect on their combat capabilities, no offense. We'll be able to provide bullet stopping, reinforced concrete, rubberized barriers, everything and anything to ensure that this place could be a safe and controlled environment for your forces."

As he was commenting, the other contractor would take off their head coverings as well. Surprisingly, she would be a woman, and out of respect for the Sal-Baliz she would only remove her goggles, keeping her helmet and mask to keep her hair from flowing out. Like Mayne, she was a pale-faced High Albic, also with almost silvery, but closer to brown hair, and deep amber eyes to match.

"Freya Moran, Deputy Operations Manager for SummitONE Solutions Shamat!" The woman loudly introduced herself, clearly the foil to Mayne's calm and collected personality. "These guns you're using too... they look like they're long overdue for maintenance, maybe we can set up ourselves some little factories here and there all over Sal-Baliz, managed and run by your own people, with materials sourcing straight out of the SummitONE inventory... y'know, so there's no risk of things blowing up when it matters the most?"

As the two contractors made their statements, Xavier Almstedt turned to the supreme leader to gauge his reaction.

"Not bad, huh? These two combined are some of the best that SummitONE Solutions has to offer. They've each served in dozens of international security contracts and domestic assignments, so they know what they're talkinga bout. What do you think, Mr. Mandhir?"
